items.title: Four evidence classes for Computer Use reports
items.statement: Computer Use reports are categorized into one of four evidence classes: real-runtime, fault-injection, hermetic-protocol, or static-contract.
items.quote: Computer Use reports use one of four evidence classes.

items.title: Real-runtime evidence requirements
items.statement: Real-runtime evidence must include complete/end_turn, policy provenance, exact identities, budget compliance, PID/window ownership, observation lineage, action sequence, dispatch evidence, and passing assertions.
items.quote: A live provider used the production Runtime, Computer Use tool, owned fixture, and executor path. Provider qualification additionally requires: - `complete/end_turn`; - enforced or explicitly reported policy provenance; - exact provider, model, producer, and live transport identity; - successful or scenario-expected actions within pre-dispatch budgets; - fixture process-instance PID/window ownership for every targeted action, including both old and replacement instances in restart scenarios; - observation lineage for every observation-bound action; - the scenario's exact action sequence when one is declared; - AX or semantic dispatch evidence for mutations; - passing expected-state and forbidden-effect assertions.

items.title: Fault-injection cannot satisfy real-runtime qualification
items.statement: Fault-injection reports are useful for regression but cannot meet real-runtime provider qualification criteria.
items.quote: Fault-injection reports are useful regression evidence but cannot satisfy a `real-runtime` provider qualification cell.

items.title: Hermetic-protocol evidence scope

items.title: Graph is a schedule, not a runtime
items.statement: The graph layer coordinates existing runtime components without duplicating execution logic.
items.quote: Graph is a durable schedule over Runtime facts, not a second execution universe.

items.title: Child Sessions as operator containers
items.statement: Each child Session acts as a reusable operator container in the graph.
items.quote: child Session → operator container

items.title: Committed RuntimeEvents as graph records
items.statement: Only committed RuntimeEvents are treated as durable graph records.
items.quote: Only committed RuntimeEvents become graph records.

items.rationale: Ensures deterministic and non-duplicative execution.
items.title: Readiness and admission separation
items.statement: Readiness must be a deterministic projection, while admission is a SQLite decision.
items.quote: Readiness is a deterministic projection; admission is a SQLite decision.

items.title: Swarm is an orchestration mode
items.statement: Agent Swarm is an orchestration mode that instructs the main Agent to use the durable asynchronous Agent Graph for independent work supervision.
items.quote: Agent Swarm is an orchestration mode, not a tool. When a Session runs in swarm mode, the main Agent is instructed to prefer the durable asynchronous Agent Graph whenever a request splits into independent work, and to supervise that graph asynchronously instead of blocking on it.

items.title: No agent_swarm tool exists
items.statement: There is no `agent_swarm` tool; it was removed in favor of asynchronous supervision over the graph.
items.quote: There is no `agent_swarm` tool. A synchronous fan-out tool of that name existed until #2384, which removed it in favour of asynchronous supervision over the graph.

items.rationale: Swarm mode biases the Agent toward fan-out for every new request, but parallelism should not be manufactured unnecessarily.
items.title: Avoid unnecessary parallelism in swarm mode
items.statement: Do not create duplicate busywork or manufacture parallelism merely because swarm mode is enabled.
items.quote: do not manufacture parallelism or create duplicate busywork merely because swarm mode is enabled.

items.rationale: Swarm mode requires specific tools to be available for the Agent to use.
items.title: Guaranteed tools in swarm mode
items.statement: Swarm mode forces `agent_list`, `update_agent_graph`, `yield_agent_graph`, `agent_swarm_status`, and `agent_output` into the turn's tool catalog.
items.quote: The mode forces `agent_list`, `update_agent_graph`, `yield_agent_graph`, `agent_swarm_status` and `agent_output` into the turn's tool catalog.

items.title: Enable swarm mode
items.statement: Swarm mode can be enabled or disabled using `/swarm on` or `/swarm off` commands, respectively.
items.quote: `/swarm on` | Set the Session orchestration mode to `swarm`
